questions.question: The minimum sea surface temperature needed for a tropical cyclone to form is about:
options: Twenty-six and a half to twenty-seven degrees Celsius

questions.question: Tropical cyclones never form on the equator because:
options: The water there is too cold
There is no water vapour at the equator
The trade winds are too strong there
The Coriolis force is zero on the equator, so converging air cannot be set spinning

questions.question: The same type of storm is called a hurricane, a typhoon or a cyclone depending on:
options: The ocean region where it occurs

questions.question: Tropical cyclones in the south-west Indian Ocean occur mainly from:
options: November to April, the warm season
All year round with no season

subtopics.title: Stages of Growth and the Anatomy of the Storm

questions.question: A system is officially classified as a tropical cyclone when sustained winds exceed:
options: One hundred and eighteen kilometres per hour

questions.question: The eye of a tropical cyclone is calm and clear because:
options: Air is sinking there, and sinking air warms, dries and dissolves cloud
It is above the ocean's coldest water
The winds cancel each other out
Rain has washed the air clean

questions.question: The strongest winds and heaviest rain in a tropical cyclone are found in the:
The self-feeding loop that powers the storm works because condensation in the eye wall:
options: Releases latent heat, deepening the low and pulling the inward spiral harder

subtopics.title: The Weather Sequence and Why the Storm Dies

questions.question: Historically, the biggest killer in tropical cyclones has been:
options: The storm surge drowning low-lying coasts

questions.question: Why is leaving shelter when the eye passes overhead so dangerous?
options: The eye contains the strongest winds
The air in the eye is toxic
The far eye wall arrives within the hour, with full violence and the wind reversed in direction
The storm surge occurs only in the eye

questions.question: A tropical cyclone weakens rapidly after landfall mainly because:
options: Its supply of warm ocean water — the source of latent heat — is cut off, and surface friction slows the winds
The Coriolis force disappears over land
The air over land is too warm

questions.question: During the approach phase, before the storm arrives, a coastal town first notices:
options: Rising swell at sea, thickening high cloud and squalls in pulses from the outer bands

subtopics.title: Case Study, Satellite Identification and Management

questions.question: Cyclone Freddy's second landfall in Mozambique in 2023 was possible because the storm:
options: Looped back over the warm Mozambique Channel and refuelled on latent heat
Was pushed back by the Kalahari High

questions.question: On a satellite image, the feature that distinguishes a mature tropical cyclone from a mid-latitude cyclone is:
options: A tight near-circular spiral with a dark central eye, rather than an open comma with trailing fronts
Its position south of forty degrees

questions.question: Freddy's worst death toll occurred in Malawi largely because of:
options: Extreme rainfall causing floods and mudslides on deforested slopes

questions.question: Preserving coastal mangrove belts is a management strategy because mangroves:
options: Act as a natural break against the storm surge
Cool the ocean below cyclone threshold

subtopics.title: The Pot, the Spin and the Birth Rules

questions.question: In the boiling-pot picture, the cyclone's petrol is:
options: Latent heat released when water vapour condenses back into cloud
The cold air above the storm

questions.question: The netball player pulling her arms in explains:
options: Why air spiralling inward toward the low spins faster and faster
Why the ocean must be warm

questions.question: Strong upper-level winds prevent a cyclone from forming because they:
options: Knock the growing storm tower over, like flicking a stack of blocks

subtopics.title: The Doughnut With the Hole in the Middle

questions.question: In the doughnut picture, the ring of dough around the hole represents:
options: The eye wall, the storm's most violent zone

questions.question: The rain bands cross a coastal town as:
options: Pulses of squall and breather, each band worse as the centre approaches
Dry gusty winds with no rain

questions.question: The sudden blue sky in the middle of the storm is a trap because:
options: It is the hole in the doughnut — the far eye wall follows within the hour, wind reversed
It signals the storm is over
The surge arrives during the calm

questions.question: The storm surge is compared to fizzy drink rising in a shaken bottle because:
options: The rain fizzes on the hot ground
Low pressure lets the sea bulge upward, and the wind then drives that bulge ashore

subtopics.title: Freddy, the Fuel Gauge and Being Ready

questions.question: Learning Freddy as a fuel story means remembering that the storm:
options: Strengthened over warm water and weakened over land, refuelling when it looped back over the channel
Was powered by strong upper winds

questions.question: The one-look identification rule from space is:
options: Both storms look identical from space
Circle with a dot is tropical; comma with a tail is mid-latitude
Comma with a tail is tropical; circle with a dot is mid-latitude
Tropical cyclones are invisible to satellites

questions.question: After the wind has gone, the first management priority is:
options: Clean water, because cholera kills after the storm has passed

questions.question: The sentence 'the storm is natural, but the size of the disaster is human' refers to:
options: Floodplain housing, deforested hills and weak warnings turning the same storm into a far bigger tragedy
